card_surface: GitHub Projects v2 is field-driven and data-table-first rather than card-first — the canonical view is the spreadsheet-style Table, and the Board view derives its card content from the same field list. As of November 2025, new projects ship with 'Linked pull requests' and 'Sub-issues progress' enabled as default fields, so PR state and child-progress are visible out-of-the-box on the card face without configuration. On a Board card the Linked pull requests field renders as one or more compact PR pills containing the GitHub PR state icon and the PR number (e.g. a purple merged-arrow + '#1234', a green open-circle + '#1234', a grey draft-circle + '#1234', or a red closed-circle + '#1234'). PR state is encoded in colour by GitHub's universal four-state convention: green = Open, purple = Merged, grey = Draft, red = Closed-without-merge. Multiple PRs render as multiple pills side-by-side rather than collapsing to a count. Sub-issue progress appears as a thin progress bar with an 'N/M' count (e.g. '3/8') or a percentage pill, depending on the configured display option. The card also surfaces whatever fields the project owner has chosen to show — Status (single-select pill in its configured colour), Issue Type (Bug / Feature / Task / Epic — coloured pill with icon, GA April 2025), Assignees (avatar stack), Labels (rounded coloured chips), Milestone, Iteration, Reviewers (avatar stack for PRs). The card surface is therefore configurable rather than opinionated — it can be minimal (status pill only) or dense (8+ fields). There is no CI/checks badge and no branch name on the card face by default.
detail_panel: GitHub does not use a slide-in panel inside Projects — opening a card opens the underlying Issue or PR view, which is the full GitHub issue page (either in place via the side-sheet item drawer or as a navigation away). The item drawer (a right-side panel inside the project view) shows all project fields stacked vertically: Title, Assignees, Labels, Milestone, Status, Linked pull requests, Parent issue, Sub-issues progress, Reviewers, Issue type, Repository, plus any custom fields. The Linked pull requests row renders each PR with its number, state icon+colour (open/draft/merged/closed), title, and head -> base branch where shown. The Reviewers row shows reviewer avatars and approval state when present (read-only as of 2025; write access was on the roadmap). Sub-issues progress shows the progress bar plus the explicit ratio and percentage. The full Issue page (clicked through from the drawer) is where commit list, CI/check runs, deployment timeline, conversation, and the Development sidebar live — Development sidebar on the issue shows successfully linked branches and PRs with their state icons; on the PR page itself the Checks tab lists every CI run with pass/fail. Test runs are not native — they appear only via third-party check integrations surfaced through the Checks API, not as a structured Tests tab inside Projects.
state_coupling: GitHub Projects v2 ships with built-in workflows (called 'Automations' in the project settings) that couple PR/issue events to the Status field. The defaults: 'Item added to project' -> Status = Todo; 'Item closed' -> Status = Done; 'Pull request merged' -> Status = Done; 'Auto-close issue' workflow closes an issue when its project Status is set to a chosen value (commonly Done). Each workflow is opt-in toggled on/off in project settings, with a configurable target Status value per workflow. Granularity is per-project (a workflow applies to all items in that project) rather than per-repo or per-branch — but because items can come from many repos into one project, the project becomes the granularity unit. As of 2025 there is no built-in default workflow for 'PR marked ready for review' -> Status = In Review or 'PR marked draft' -> Status = In Progress — these are the top community feature requests (Discussion #159684). Teams that need that coupling today use the GitHub Actions Projects API to write custom workflows that listen for the pull_request.ready_for_review and pull_request.converted_to_draft events and call the GraphQL mutation to update the item's Status. A separate repository-level setting (added April 2025) controls whether merging a linked PR auto-closes its linked issue (default on, can be disabled per repo) — this is independent of the Projects workflow and operates at the issue level.
draft_vs_ready_state: Draft vs. Ready is first-class in GitHub's data model and propagates into Projects v2 visually but not (by default) into status transitions. On the card face and in the drawer, the Linked pull requests pill uses GitHub's universal draft-PR icon: a grey/open hollow circle with a smaller filled circle inside (the 'draft' glyph), versus the green filled open-PR icon when ready for review. The colour difference (grey for draft, green for open/ready) is the primary visual cue. As of the 2025 changelog, GitHub added the converted_from_draft event to the Projects v2 item timeline — alongside project_v2_item_status_changed, added_to_project_v2, and removed_from_project_v2 — so the draft->ready transition is now a queryable, auditable event in the project's item history (visible in the issue/PR Timeline and via the GraphQL API). However, no built-in project automation fires on that event by default; teams must build a Workflow via GitHub Actions if they want Status to advance from 'In Progress' to 'In Review' when a PR moves out of draft. The community feature request to add this as a built-in workflow trigger remains open. Draft PRs still appear on the card (no hiding by default), and counted in Linked pull requests; the visual signal is icon colour alone.
review_state: Reviewers are surfaced on the card via a dedicated 'Reviewers' field that can be enabled in the project's field list — once on, it renders as an avatar stack on the Board card and as a row in the item drawer. It shows requested reviewers and reviewers who have submitted reviews; approval state is implicit rather than explicit (the field is read-only and does not surface a '2/2 approved' count on the card face). Approvals, change-requests, and the full review thread live on the PR page itself, not in Projects. Blocking reviews are not flagged separately on the project card. Users have reported the Reviewers field rendering inconsistently — sometimes only a subset of reviewers appears (community Discussion #171268). The Linked pull requests pill itself encodes only PR state (open/draft/merged/closed), not review status. There is no built-in default to surface 'review requested on me' on a card; that workflow is owned by GitHub's Reviews inbox and the @mentions/notifications system outside Projects.
dod_checklist: GitHub Projects v2 has no first-class Definition of Done checklist field. Teams use markdown task lists in the issue body, which GitHub treats specially: GitHub auto-calculates and displays a 'tasks completed' progress (e.g. '3 of 5 tasks completed') in the issues list and in repository views. Tasklists (the more structured beta feature from earlier years) were largely superseded by the 2025 sub-issues GA — sub-issues are now the canonical structured-breakdown primitive. Sub-issues are themselves full issues with their own status, assignee, labels, and progress, and roll up to a parent via the Sub-issues progress field, which renders as a progress bar/pill at the parent level (configurable: bar, pill, or fraction). Task lists in markdown still work and still show a percentage in some contexts, but they do not appear on the project card. DoD does not gate state transitions natively — there is no rule preventing a story from being moved to Done while sub-issues remain open. On the card face, sub-issue progress is the closest thing to a DoD indicator (and is enabled by default for new projects as of November 2025). Per-issue-type templated DoD checklists are not built-in; teams can pre-populate via Issue Templates (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/) per repo.
test_linkage: GitHub Projects v2 has no native test management. Test linkage flows through the Checks API: any CI provider can post check runs against a commit (the same surface GitHub Actions uses for its workflow runs), and those check runs appear on the PR's Checks tab as pass/fail/in-progress rows. Test results from third-party tools (e.g. Playwright, Jest, Cypress, JUnit) surface only as check runs unless a dedicated GitHub App parses and pushes structured test data. There is no Tests tab inside a Project, no coverage badge on cards, and no pass/fail count field. CI pass/fail is therefore a separate axis from Linked pull requests in the Projects data model — it lives on the PR page's Checks tab, not on the project card. Third-party test management tools (Xray, TestRail, Zephyr) integrate at the repo level via GitHub Apps and add their data to the PR/issue surface but not as native Projects fields. Quality/coverage signals on a project card can only be approximated by custom single-select fields ('QA Status: Passed / Failed') or by status-field automations driven by Actions workflows.
cicd_status: CI/CD status is not surfaced on the project card. CI lives on the PR page in the Checks tab (each workflow run is a row with pass/fail/queued/cancelled icons in GitHub's standard colours: green check / red x / yellow dot / grey dash) and on commit pages as small status icons. The Linked pull requests pill on a project card shows PR open/draft/merged/closed state but does not aggregate or surface the underlying CI verdict — a PR pill stays green-open even with all checks failing. There is no built-in 'CI failing' badge or 'checks: 5/6 passed' indicator on cards. The Status field in Projects does not advance on check success/failure by default; users wanting that behaviour wire it via GitHub Actions calling the Projects GraphQL mutation. A repo's Settings -> Branches required-status-checks govern whether a PR can merge, which transitively gates the project's PR-merged -> Done workflow, but this is invisible at the card level. CI/CD providers supported by the Checks API include GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Buildkite, Travis, Jenkins (via app), Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, and any service implementing the Checks API.
release_tagging: Release tagging in GitHub uses three overlapping primitives, none of which is a Projects-v2-native field: (1) Milestones — repo-scoped grouping with a name, due date, and progress count, surfaced as a 'Milestone' field on the project card (configurable pill); (2) Iterations — Projects v2 native field for time-boxed sprints, configurable cadence and per-iteration editing, used for sprint/PI-style planning; (3) Git Releases/Tags — repo-level published releases tied to a git tag and commit SHA, NOT exposed as a Projects v2 field. There is no out-of-the-box 'Release' or 'Fix Version' field equivalent to Jira's Fix Version or Linear's Releases pipeline. Teams that need release tracking inside Projects v2 typically: (a) use Milestone as the release container (one Milestone per release), (b) add a custom Single Select field 'Release' with options like '1.4.0 / 1.5.0', or (c) use Iteration as a hybrid sprint+release. Multiple-release membership is not natively modelled — an issue has exactly one Milestone, though it can sit in many Projects. Release scope changes are tracked only via the Milestone re-assignment event in the issue timeline; there is no first-class scope-change audit. On the card, Milestone and Iteration both render as pills when their fields are enabled. [uncertain: there may be newer release-pipeline features in late 2025/2026 that the search results did not surface.]
aggregation: Aggregation in GitHub Projects v2 is sub-issue-driven, not PR-driven. The Sub-issues progress field aggregates child-issue status into the parent, rendering as a progress bar/pill showing 'N of M completed' or a percentage; this is the only roll-up built into the card face. It rolls up issue status (open/closed) not PR/branch/CI state — so a parent showing '5/5' means all child issues are closed, not that all child PRs are merged. There is no native 'X of N child stories have merged PRs' rollup, no aggregated CI rollup, and no aggregated branch/PR count at the parent level. Issue Types (GA April 2025) and the parent/sub-issue hierarchy (up to 8 levels deep, 100 sub-issues per parent) enable Epic/Feature/Story-style breakdowns, and the Roadmap view can group by parent issue to show hierarchical progress bars — but the progress shown is always status-based, not VCS-based. Aggregation across multiple repos works because Projects v2 spans repositories, but the rollup unit remains the parent-issue. This is consistently identified as a gap: the Linked pull requests field exists on the parent card, but it shows only the parent's own linked PRs, never an aggregated child-PR rollup.
environment_deployment_target: Environments are first-class in GitHub at the repo/Actions level but are not exposed as a Projects v2 card field. GitHub's Deployments API and Environments (Settings -> Environments) let workflows record deployments to named targets (e.g. production, staging, preview); the most recent deployment for an environment is shown on the repository home, on the Environments page, and in the PR conversation when a workflow deploys from a PR branch. The PR page surfaces deployment status as an inline 'Deployed to staging' indicator with timestamp and URL. Inside Projects v2, however, none of this is a structured field — there is no 'Environment' field, no 'Deployed to' pill on cards, and no built-in environment-progression timeline. Teams approximate this by adding a custom Single Select field ('Environment: dev / staging / prod') and updating it via GitHub Actions workflow_run / deployment_status events posting to the Projects GraphQL API. Vercel, Netlify, and similar preview-environment apps post check runs that surface on the PR Checks tab but not on the project card. Multi-environment progression (dev -> staging -> prod) is therefore manual or scripted, not native.
traceability_completeness: GitHub Projects v2 does not surface a composite traceability indicator. There is no badge, ring, or icon strip that reads 'code merged + tests passed + deployed + DoD complete' as a single card-level signal. Each axis lives on a separate field or a separate page: Linked pull requests (card field, PR state only), Sub-issues progress (card field, status-only rollup), CI checks (PR page, not Projects), Deployments (PR page / repo Environments, not Projects), DoD (markdown checklist in issue body, not Projects). The closest approximation is the Status field itself — combined with the 'PR merged -> Status = Done' built-in workflow, reaching Done implies a merged PR; but Status doesn't formally encode tests-passed, deployed, or DoD-met. Some teams build their own composite via a custom Number or Single Select field updated by an Action that watches all the relevant events, but this is not built-in. Incomplete traceability does not gate state transitions natively. GitHub's stance leans toward explicit per-axis signals (matching Linear's philosophy) rather than a composite indicator, consistent with the broader 'field-driven, data-table-first' philosophy of Projects v2 — the user composes the view they want by toggling fields, rather than seeing a pre-computed traceability badge.
design_pattern: The GitHub Projects v2 design pattern is field-driven, data-table-first, and visually flat. The canonical view is the Table (spreadsheet) — Board, Roadmap, and the new layouts all derive from the same field set, so 'card design' really means 'which fields are visible and in what order'. PR state is encoded by GitHub's universal PR-state icon vocabulary (filled circle = open / hollow circle with inner dot = draft / merged arrow = merged / red circle with slash = closed) with paired colours (green / grey / purple / red); the icon-and-colour pair is the atomic unit and is consistent across PR pages, issue Development sidebars, and project cards. On the card, each linked PR is its own pill — the pattern is 'one PR = one pill', never a single aggregated counter glyph (unlike Linear's single branch-fork icon-with-count). When no PR is linked, the field is simply absent from the card (no placeholder slot). Sub-issue progress uses a thin progress bar + optional percentage/fraction — clean, restrained, no decoration. Issue Type and Status both use named coloured pills with optional icons (Issue Type icons were introduced with the April 2025 GA). The overall vocabulary: pills for state, bars for aggregation, avatar stacks for people, icons-with-colour for PR state. The pattern is consistent across issue types (issue, PR, draft) — the same field framework applies. Compared to Linear's compressed single-glyph approach, GitHub's pattern is more verbose and more configurable; compared to Jira's icon-strip approach, GitHub's is cleaner because each field is its own pill rather than packed into a meta-strip. The design philosophy aligns with 'show the data, let the user choose what to see' rather than 'pre-compose a card layout'. For Sand/N6, the relevant takeaways are: (a) the PR-state-as-coloured-pill-with-icon vocabulary is the strongest cross-tool convention; (b) sub-issue progress bars at the parent level are now expected as default; (c) field-toggle (show/hide) is the right escape valve when card density becomes uncomfortable.
